evidence.note: After reading the reference, agent states 'This is a massive project... Let me prioritize - I'll need to be strategic' and 'focus on parity for structurally tested behaviors' — genuine intent to decompose but expressed as a vague mental list with no written milestone breakdown or per-piece completion criteria.

Wrote all subsystems as modules in a natural dependency order (db.rs/schema.sql → models → md → templates → jobs → handlers chunked by feature: accounts, posts, comments, tags, search, media, feeds, admin). Shows an implicit sensible decomposition, but built everything in a single push with no per-subsystem done-check before moving on.
Only after all modules were written did the agent build once and start reactively probing endpoints — verification was not planned as a milestone exit test but happened as a bunched post-build phase.

The foundational, high-risk shared-DB / cross-runtime schema_info migration concern was discovered reactively at the very end after the reference failed to migrate — a dependency that a dependency-aware milestone plan would have sequenced early, indicating sequencing was emergent rather than risk-tiered.
Late-stage subsystem work (markdown rel attrs, 404/405 routing, path-param parsing) handled as a reactive punch-list of parity diffs, not as pre-defined milestones with exit tests.

reasoning: The agent had a real, sensibly-ordered module decomposition (schema/db before feeds/handlers) which lifts it above a purely monolithic effort, but there was never an explicit written milestone plan with per-subsystem completion criteria; strategic statements stayed vague ('be strategic', 'prioritize'). Construction was a one-shot 'write everything then build once' push with verification bunched reactively at the end, and the riskiest shared-state interface (cross-runtime schema/migration) was discovered late rather than sequenced first. This matches the level-3 anchor ('vague mental list, no explicit completion criteria') with a partial lean toward level-5's sensible ordering and rough post-hoc done-signals, placing it at a 4.
